scope: Read-only static review of current spectator capture path and shared-owner/async execution boundaries. No live samples, private files, recordings, tests, builds, service or load were read or run.

facts.claim: Each active WebSocket owns a capture interval (default250ms, missed ticks delayed). Snapshot construction and SpectatorHub.publish execute synchronously inside tokio::task::block_in_place. The same socket session select task waits for this call; independently spawned reader/outbound tasks can continue. This is not a bare unmarked blocking publish on a Tokio worker.

Personal snapshot is built first. Shared world_snapshot then locks the same shared Zone state mutex used by movement/owner transactions, overlays visible map entities, vitals and cooldowns, and clones all other same-map player entities before dropping that lock. Final AOI retain and sort run after unlock. Subsequent spectator JSON and disk work do not retain this Zone mutex.

The snapshot overlay scans shared map entity/drop maps, filters before cloning visible map objects, and scans/clones all same-map other players. Work under Zone lock therefore grows with shared map object count plus same-map players and cloned visible payload, rather than solely this client's final AOI count.

sanitize_world executes before hub mutex. It converts the full client view to serde_json::Value, clones the source entity array before take(max_entities), and clones terrain/decor/scene/map-transfer values into the spectator value. max_entities is a per-input truncation after initial serialization/array clone, not an upfront bound on all allocation work.

WorldSnapshotClientView::serialize itself first builds a full serde_json::Value from the lossless snapshot, removes private fields, then serializes that value. The outer spectator to_value traverses this result again; snapshot inventory/system data may be materialized before spectator sanitization discards those fields.

The global spectator std::Mutex covers latest-world clone, merge, stale pruning and event diff before checking the per-map capture interval. An Ok(None) suppressed emission still performed snapshot construction, sanitization, world merge and event work. At25 ready sockets, nominal input attempts can approach25x4=100/s although a same-map emitted recording remains at most about4/s; actual rates require measurement.

Merge clones previous and next entity/drop payloads into BTreeMaps and replaces old arrays, with duplicate-ID replacement dropping prior clones. Event diff builds ID indexes. For U unique union objects, work includes O((old+new) log U) indexing and O(payload bytes/nodes) cloning and destruction. Merged entity union is not capped again by max_entities; stale pruning limits unseen retention by time, not a fixed map-wide object count.

For emitted frames, world is cloned again, JSON world/events value plus Vec encoding is produced, the2MiB encoded-payload limit is checked after allocation/encoding, SHA256 is computed, and frame.clone is retained in ring. These execute under hub mutex. The2MiB limit is not a direct in-memory Value allocation cap.

Default ring is2400 frames per map. Stable config means a new emitted frame removes at most one oldest frame after the ring fills; there is no2400-frame sweep. VecDeque removal metadata is constant-time, but discarded Frame owns a Value tree/events/strings, so its destructor frees work proportional to that frame's allocations while hub mutex remains held. Ideal4Hz needs at least about600s for2400 emits; elapsed time alone cannot prove fullness or a stall cause.

Each emitted recording synchronously create_dir_all/open(append)/JSON encode via64KiB BufWriter/newline/explicit flush/close while hub mutex remains held, inside caller's block_in_place. The buffer reduces tiny write calls but does not make file access asynchronous or add fsync/atomic-append guarantees; file/device delays remain possible and unmeasured here.

The Ok(Some(Frame)) returned by block_in_place is ignored by the caller's if-let Err branch. That returned frame's owned tree is destroyed in the outer async-task scope after the blocking closure returns. Ring-retained and returned frames are separate deep clones; this is a candidate for synchronous allocator/destructor cost outside the marked blocking closure, not evidence of actual stall duration.

Public health directly calls spectator.metrics(), which synchronously locks the global hub mutex in an async handler. A long publish/append can therefore delay health and occupy that polling thread; this is distinct from the marked publish block_in_place path.

A spectator viewer frame_at locks hub and deep-clones a frame; view transformation and JSON string generation then run in the async viewer path. This is conditional on actual viewers; no viewer presence is established by this source review. AI live defaults disabled (ai_live.rs61) and must not be blamed without runtime enablement evidence.

zone work timers start after Zone mutex acquisition and exclude snapshot read/overlay work and lock waiting. Owner/pending movement deadline lag is observed after acquiring the lock and can expose delayed scheduling/lock access. Request timing includes admitted request execution/queueing boundaries, but MovementAdmission may finish before a queued movement deadline/owner ACK. None measures network fanout delivery or pins a1.4s symptom to spectator work.

complexity.notation: B=current serialized/tree payload; U=merged unique entities+drops; P=same-map players; N=active publisher sockets
complexity.perPublisher: full personal/shared snapshot + sanitization + merge/event diff even when no frame emitted; O(B) allocation/destruction plus O(U log U) indexes, shared-map scan and O(P) remote-player clone
complexity.perMapEmit: extra O(B) deep clones/encoding/hash and synchronous append; once ring full one old-frame O(B_old allocations) destruction
complexity.memory: 2400 deep-owned frame trees per map plus latest world, clones, JSON Value/encoded Vec and pending events; serialized payload cap is not a heap byte cap

proofLimits: Source establishes possible contention and allocation/I/O boundaries only; it cannot prove the observed1.4s/fanout failure root cause.
Low average CPU or low process byte throughput does not rule out brief mutex contention, allocator latency, synchronous I/O or scheduling delays; it also does not establish them.
Need actual emit/sequence timeline to associate the first ring eviction with the failure. No live raw, large recording or private log was read for this review.
Existing failed formal02 result must remain failed; no threshold, denominator, workload or acceptance reinterpretation is made.
nextObservation: Use already-owned public failure timestamps and cumulative monitor bucket differences for the exact phase/window; do not use lifetime p99 or infer disk saturation from process Other I/O.

If separately authorized, add bounded duration/size/count observations for snapshot Zone-lock wait/hold, sanitize, hub wait/hold, merge/events, encode/hash, ring eviction destructor, append open/write/flush and returned-frame destruction. Do not expose snapshot payloads or account/secret labels.

Correlate emitted sequence/ring depth and frame encoded bytes with each slow path; an isolated PID-filtered short trace/stack sample can distinguish allocator versus file/device wait if counters still cannot.
Retain production recording, original normal read/replay semantics and all existing acceptance gates for any later fix; no Cell P2 work is authorized by this analysis.
